speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have moved this Motion because of the High Court's findings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If there is an appeal against the judgment, the Court of Appeal will decide on the merits of the appeal in due course.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Given the very serious findings about: (a) the dishonesty of particular Members of this House, and (b) the misuse and loss of public funds, the question is what is going to be done in the interim, pending the appeal, if there is one.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Will the Workers' Party provide the House with any guarantees to uphold accountability and transparency between now and the appeal?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This Motion is also about the integrity and character expected of public officials and Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It pains me to move this Motion, in particular, because one of the two Members named in it is Mr Low Thia Khiang, if I may be permitted a personal note at the outset, he is someone for whom I have always had a high regard.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I think many on both sides of the House share my sentiment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But there are important questions of public interest to consider.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will mention just a few at the outset.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Millions of dollars of public funds are involved.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Pending the appeal, if there is one, this House is entitled to ask: are Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang going to continue to have oversight and decision-making power over public funds in the Aljunied-Hougang Town Council (AHTC)?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And, what do those in charge of AHTC intend to do about the findings in the judgment?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I should add that from February 2013 to September 2015, the Town Council included Punggol East and was known AHPETC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For simplicity, I will refer to the Town Council consistently as AHTC so as not to confuse listeners.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will deal with the judgment and the questions raised following the judgment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The judgment is the latest chapter in a saga that has been eight years in the making.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Throughout this long time, the Workers' Party has consistently and repeatedly refused to take responsibility for the problems in its Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party town councillors have persistently resisted disclosure, offered countless excuses and made a litany of misleading statements – to the public, in Parliament and before the Courts.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have not been transparent in their dealings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party wanted their friends to manage their Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The honest and honourable thing to do, if one wants to appoint one's friends is: be transparent and open about it.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Disclose all the facts, so that a fair decision can be made.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And call an open tender, so that your friends compete with the market.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And this is important – you cannot allow your friends to overcharge.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What the Workers' Party did was the opposite.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They told untruths and manipulated the circumstances, so that FM Solutions and Services (FMSS) would be appointed, whatever the case.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They did not care whether FMSS was the best candidate to serve residents.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Indeed, Mr Low said that he would have appointed FMSS, even if a cheaper, more experienced contractor had put in a bid.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To guarantee FMSS' appointment, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang waived the tender, even though the law required it.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They misled their own town councillors, including their own fellow Members in the Group Representation Constituency (GRC) and gave a false reason to them for not calling a tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And they removed the existing Managing Agent (MA) and appointed their friends in FMSS, though FMSS had less experience and charged more.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This overcharging, abuse of public funds, was inexcusable.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What they did was in breach of their fiduciary duties, at every turn.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They told untruths and distorted the facts and knowingly sacrificed their residents' interests in favour of their friends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: After having misled their own town councillors to get FMSS appointed without a tender, they then repeatedly misled the public and Parliament on why they had hired their friends in this manner.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They misled their own auditors, too, and refused to give them documents which would have revealed the truth.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is a tale of deception, spun out over eight years, which finally unravelled in Court, and not just in one Court.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It unravelled in three different Courts, including the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Under the management of the Workers' Party's friends, the Town Council ran up deficits.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Allowing your friends to help themselves to public funds – that is a tale that belongs to the Third World, not Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In two different trials, the Courts reached judgments that showed that the Workers' Party's Members of Parliament had misled Parliament – first in 2015, and now, in the latest judgment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even so, the Workers' Party maintains that they are not answerable either to the Courts or to Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Indeed, they have taken the position in Court that as elected Members of Parliament, they are not answerable to the Courts for any serious mismanagement or mis-spending of public funds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Both the High Court and the Court of Appeal disagreed with this submission, which sought to place the Workers' Party Members above the law.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It was a remarkable position for the Workers' Party to take.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They are saying that no matter what wrongs they commit and no matter how much public funds are misused, they are not answerable and nothing can be done to them in Court.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This was said in the hope that the electorate would not pay attention to their wrongdoings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Therefore, everything could be covered up and forgotten.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The auditors raised serious questions about the adequacy of the Town Council's financial and accounting systems.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The responsible thing for Ms Sylvia Lim, the Workers' Party Town Council Chairman then, to have done at that moment, was to come clean, accept that there were issues, and fix them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the next audit in 2014, they hid details of the transactions with their friends, and refused to give the documents and information to their own auditors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The auditors were alarmed and again issued a disclaimer of opinion on the Accounts.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The AGO report stated that despite repeated requests for critical documents, the Town Council did not produce them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Parliament debated the AGO report in February 2015.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even at that point, instead of taking ownership and rectifying the problems uncovered by AGO, the Workers' Party Members – and Ms Sylvia Lim in particular – made excuses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They repeated in this House their objections to the AGO report, objections which the AGO had already addressed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Instead of dealing with the issues, they sought to obfuscate, throw doubt on AGO, pretend that everything was fine.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Law Minister said in this House that the conduct of Ms Sylvia Lim and her fellow town councillors was unlawful and that they were in breach of their fiduciary duties.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim's response was to shout "Rubbish", brazenly denying their unacceptable actions using unparliamentary language.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Despite their refusal to acknowledge the issues, then Minister of National Development, Mr Khaw Boon Wan, patiently advised the Workers' Party to take immediate steps to resolve the problems.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: He urged them to take concrete steps to recover the losses and make restitution to their residents.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Sadly, the Workers' Party did not do anything.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I do not know what they were expecting.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Perhaps, they felt that somehow the public would forget and give them a free pass since they were an Opposition party.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They were not used to running a GRC, so the public would "give chance".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Indeed, shortcomings resulting from inexperience can be forgotten.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But dishonesty, deliberate and repeated deception, to profit one's friends, cannot be forgiven, or swept under the carpet.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We would not be here today speaking about these judgments, if the Workers' Party, and Ms Sylvia Lim in particular, had even at this late stage in 2015, been serious about setting things straight.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If they had corrected the problems, got their friends to make good the losses, it could all have been very different.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But the Workers' Party refused to acknowledge the issues and flatly refused to deal with them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Both the High Court and the Court of Appeal took a serious view of the matter.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Tellingly, both had sharp remarks about the Workers' Party's conduct.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help Members follow the Courts' findings, I wish to distribute Annex 2 – Quotes from the Judgments – to my speech.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The High Court observed that Ms Sylvia Lim's statement in Parliament in 2015 that the Town Council had done due transfers to the sinking fund was curious because of what she had failed to mention.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Court described Ms Sylvia Lim's behaviour with the Latin phrase "suppressio veri, suggestio falsi" – suppression of the truth is equivalent to the suggestion of what is false.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Thus, the Court had already taken a view on this matter as early as 2015, after the AGO report was debated in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Court of Appeal ordered the Town Council to appoint independent accountants, despite the Workers' Party's resistance.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: AHTC then responded to the Court of Appeal's order cynically, nominating accountants to do the forensic audit, but failing to provide enough information on their proposed accountants’ experience and expertise.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When HDB asked for additional information, AHTC did not respond.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Court of Appeal noted the Town Council's lack of rigour and basic due diligence in how it nominated accountants.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On the Court of Appeal’s direction, AHTC eventually appointed KPMG LLP (KPMG).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Among them: One, that the Town Council had not been justified to waive tender before appointing FMSS as its MA.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There were conflicts of interest in the Town Council's appointment of FMSS and FM Solutions and Integrated Services (FMSI).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: FMSI, which was engaged by the Town Council to provide essential maintenance and lift rescue services, was a sole proprietorship owned by the Secretary of the Town Council, who was also part-owner of FMSS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The people that formed FMSS and FMSI were the Workers' Party’s friends – trusted, loyal supporters.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: FMSS' directors and shareholders were the Secretary, General Manager and Deputy General Manager of AHTC, respectively.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Town Councillors relinquished an unacceptably high degree of financial responsibility to conflicted persons.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: All of the payments to FMSS/FMSI were co-signed by the conflicted persons.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There were overpayments to FMSS, and payments to FMSS without certification of work performed or without the requisite co-signature of members of the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There were also numerous breaches of the Town Councils Act and Town Council Financial Rules.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the meantime, PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) – retained by Pasir Ris-Punggol Town Council (PRPTC) after Punggol East became part of PRPTC after the 2015 General Election – submitted its own report.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Again, it found that AHTC had not been transparent, and had delayed granting PwC access to all necessary documents and information.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In view of these serious flaws, the Court of Appeal then directed the Town Council to appoint an independent panel to take such action as may be appropriate to safeguard residents' interests.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers’ Party chose the Members of the Independent PaneI.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Pritam Singh, on behalf of AHTC, welcomed the appointments and called the independent members "eminent", as, indeed, they were.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Chaired by Mr Philip Jeyaretnam Senior Counsel, the other two members of the Independent Panel were Mr N Sreenivasan Senior Counsel and Mr Ong Pang Thye, Managing Partner of KPMG.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Independent Panel went through the facts and concluded that the Town Council’s monies had been wrongly spent.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On behalf of the Town Council, it decided to sue the key persons involved, including Mr Low Thia Khiang, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Pritam Singh, for losses arising from wrongful payments by the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It was the Independent Panel that did so.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Independent Panel appointed by AHTC, acting on behalf of AHTC, sued AHTC's councillors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party has persistently refused over eight years to be transparent about what it had done.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At numerous points over the last eight years, they could have acted.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2013, they could have acted after their own auditors issued reports, before the AGO stepped in.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2015, they could have acted when AGO made its report and Parliament debated the matter.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In 2016 and 2017, they could have acted when KPMG and PwC issued their reports.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But, at every turn, at every turn of the way, there was obfuscation instead of transparency, resistance instead of accountability, denial instead of honesty.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Hence, the matter came before the Courts to decide.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Following a 17-day trial, the Court issued a 329-page judgment, which established the following important facts and conclusions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Court found that Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim had deliberately delayed calling a tender in order to provide themselves with a convenient, but false, excuse to waive the tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the trial, the Workers' Party accepted that they only needed two months to call a tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They could have asked CPG, the previous MA, to continue providing MA services for far longer than that.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They had ample time to call for a tender, but deliberately delayed doing so, in order to create an excuse not to call a tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In fact, the Court found that there had never been any intention to call a tender in the first place.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They admitted in Court that they had decided to engage FMSS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They also admitted that they had rejected other parties who were interested in providing MA services.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As I said earlier, if one wants to appoint one's friends, there is a proper, transparent process to do so.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party deliberately chose the wrong way, and the two hid the truth from their own town councillors and the public.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Among the Workers' Party town councillors, they had one experienced town councillor who had been Chairman of another Town Council for 20 years and they had three lawyers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They should have known that a tender could only be waived under very special circumstances, and they should also have known that these special circumstances did not exist when they waived tender in this case.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If they had called a tender and their trusted friends had been the only bidders, they could then have appointed their friends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even if there had been several bids, they could have still chosen to appoint their friends, provided they acted honestly and properly: explain why they were appointing their friends, record the reasons in the Minutes and be prepared to defend the reasons in public.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But they admitted in Court that if a tender had been called, there was a risk that someone else might have put in a bid.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Indeed, there were other parties that had expressed an interest to provide MA services to AHTC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They admitted that if someone had put in a bid better than FMSS', they would have been duty-bound to consider the bid.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And they knew that FMSS would not have got the job if they had said they would only accept the better bid.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, they were not prepared to take the risk that would have come from being honest: appoint their friends despite receiving better bids from others; and explain to the public why they have done so.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But they were prepared to run the risk that came from being dishonest.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, they claimed they had no time to call a tender, so that they could appoint FMSS without a tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As I said, the right way was to go before the tender and contracts committee to justify the decision to appoint their friends, and have their reasons documented.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Furthermore – and this is extremely important – if they want to appoint their friends, then they should have made sure that their friends charged less – and not more – than their previous MA.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The previous MA was an established institution, while their friends had set up a fledgling company, which, as they admitted in Court, had no experience in managing a town the size of AHTC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It means they knew that what they were doing was wrong, but nevertheless persisted in the wrong.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And they deliberately set out to mislead everyone, including their own colleagues in the Town Council, so as to hide their wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Annex 3 is a compilation of the Workers' Party's misleading statements.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party misled their own Town Councillors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They deliberately kept the decision to appoint FMSS away from a Town Council meeting.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Instead they delegated authority to Ms Sylvia Lim, so as to keep the other town councillors in the dark.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They concealed their true motives from the rest of the town councillors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Danny Loh was asked to draft the report.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms How Weng Fan and Mr Danny Loh were the very officers and shareholders whose appointment was to be approved without tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And here were Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim asking them to draft the comment on a report concerning their own appointment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Judge considered this to be extraordinary and stated these actions cast serious doubt on their honesty and integrity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Judge found that this misled the public and the very constituents the Members of Parliament were elected to serve.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As the Judge put it, and I quote, "There was a concerted attempt to cloak the appointment of FMSS with a veneer of propriety", "in order to camouflage its true motive".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The press release also falsely asserted that AHTC did not incur additional MA fees from appointing FMSS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She then had to agree that she had lied in the press release, which was disseminated to all Singaporeans, including the residents of AHTC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim said in Parliament in 2015, I quote, "For the first contract in 2011 for MA services, it was triggered as the incumbent MA, CPG Facilities Management, asked to be released from the contract with the Town Council for business reasons.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There was an urgent need to put in place a computer system due to the termination of the former system in use." The judgment was crystal clear on this, and I quote, "There was no urgency or public interest that warranted the waiver of tender.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It was neither CPG Facilities Management's announcement on 30 May 2011 nor Action Information Management Pte Ltd (AIM's) withdrawal of the Town Council Management System (TCMS) that resulted in tender being waived." In waiving tender, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang's, and I quote, "conduct was improper and the attempt to cloak the same with a veneer of truth and credibility collectively leads to the conclusion that they had not acted honestly".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When one reads the record – the AGO report, the KPMG report, the PwC reports, three Court judgments – you will find misleading statements made by the Workers' Party Members of Parliament piling up.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In sum, waiver of tender was not justified but they did this to appoint their friends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They knew that this was wrong and thus misled their own town councillors, misled their own auditors, misled the public and misled Parliament to hide their wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang not only misled Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They also knowingly allowed Mr Pritam Singh to mislead Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Pritam Singh said in 2015, and I quote, "Where FMSS is a tenderer in a tender called by the Town Council, as was the case in 2011 for the MA contract, FMSS is kept at an arm's length and a China wall is built between FMSS and the Town Council".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Court found How Weng Fan had been heavily involved since early May 2011, soon after the General Election, in setting up FMSS and in the plot to keep CPG in the dark.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: She was even involved in the preparation of the FMSS letter of intent and, as I noted earlier, in sanitising the report on FMSS' appointment as MA, for the auditors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang knew very well they had not kept How at arm’s length.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Yet, they let Mr Pritam Singh mislead this House without correcting him.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When the Workers' Party leaders let their own Members of Parliament mislead Parliament on their behalf, what does this say about the Workers' Party's integrity and values?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers’ Party also misled Parliament that their safeguards for transactions with their friends were adequate.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim told this House in 2015, and I quote, "It was the policy that no cheque to FMSS of whatever amount could be issued unless either the Town Council Chairman or one of the Vice Chairmen co-signed the cheque.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Thus, it was not possible for FMSS to pay itself unless it was authorised by the Town Council Chair or Vice Chair who have no interest in FMSS whatsoever." Mr Png Eng Huat said, and I quote, "Our MA cannot make payments to themselves for the above services without the Chairman or one of the Vice Chairmen to co-sign the cheque." These are half-truths at best because, in reality, there was no standing instruction that co-signatures were required on cheques for payments to FMSI, the EMSU provider.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim admitted to the Court that she did not personally check that each payment was justified.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Despite all the reassurances they gave, there were payments to FMSS without the requisite co-signature of members of the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim remains a Vice Chairman of AHTC while Mr Low Thia Khiang is a member of AHTC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: More than three weeks have passed since the Court judgment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party has been totally silent on this matter.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is why I have to ask in Parliament, what does the current Chairman of AHTC Mr Faisal Manap intend to do?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the minimum, will he apologise to residents of Aljunied and Hougang for letting them down?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: An apology would be the first step, a belated recognition that they had let residents down and an intention to put things right.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Very serious adverse findings were made against them – findings that go to the heart of the integrity of these Members of Parliament and the deceptive manner in which they conducted the Town Council’s affairs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: How can they remain in charge of the Town Council's affairs as if it is business as usual?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the very least, should not the Chairman and other town councillors require them to recuse themselves from handling the Town Council’s financial matters, as called for in this Motion?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Or will he allow her to continue to be in a position where she can co-sign cheques on behalf of AHTC?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If AHTC were a company, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang would, at the very least, have been interdicted – prohibited or restrained from acting – pending their appeal.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Most likely, they would have been forced to leave the company a long time ago – when AGO and then KPMG made their findings – instead of being allowed to carry on, in the same roles and enjoying the same degree of financial oversight over public funds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If they were members of a professional body – and many Members of this House are members of professional bodies – their acts of dishonesty would have brought them before a disciplinary tribunal.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As the earlier judgment of the High Court noted, they might have been exposed to civil liability or, in an extreme scenario, to criminal liability.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In light of how they have misled this House and the absence of a response by the Town Council, I would like to know what, if anything, the Workers' Party's remaining Members of Parliament and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament propose to do about these findings pending any appeal.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Will they at long last be conducting their own investigations or will they continue to duck, dodge and deny?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As Secretary-General and Chairman, respectively, of the Workers' Party, Mr Pritam Singh and Ms Sylvia Lim are responsible for party standards and discipline.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Both are themselves involved in the AHTC problem.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But it is still their duty to act for the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Will they apologise on behalf of the Workers' Party?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Will they direct Mr Faisal Manap to do the right thing to protect AHTC's governance?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Will they temporarily stand aside themselves and allow some other Workers' Party's Central Executive Committee (CEC) member to take charge of this matter, again, a standard practice in the corporate world?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If nothing is done from now till the appeal is concluded, we will be forced to conclude that the Workers' Party, by its inaction, in fact, endorses the dishonest conduct and the breach of the fiduciary duties that have already occurred and is complicit in the wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I hope that the Workers' Party will take action.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There were other financial and governance lapses which occurred in AHTC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party has put them right, albeit after a very long delay and after denying and resisting for many years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In doing so, the Workers' Party has shown that they are, in fact, capable of taking steps to put their house in order when further obfuscation and delay at last become untenable.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have detailed earlier how the Workers' Party initially resisted the appointment of any independent auditor, then resisted the appointment of a Big Four accounting firm.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Almost two years after KMPG was appointed, AHTC finally cleared the audit.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am sure that the town councillors will agree that they are the better for the audit and that their controls and processes are now much safer.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Sometimes, a bitter pill has to be taken so a sick system can be returned to health.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Similarly, now that honesty, integrity, candour and transparency of some of the most senior Workers' Party members have been called into serious question – by the High Court no less – will the Workers' Party be willing to swallow another bitter pill and take action?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If the Workers' Party wants the privilege of representing Singaporeans in Parliament, they cannot be silent on this.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Beyond the specific facts of this case, this episode reminds us of the need for integrity and probity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We hope that the Workers' Party Members of Parliament, and all Non-Constituency Members of Parliament and Nominated Members of Parliament, will agree that Members of Parliament should be held to the following standards in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Members of Parliament should not mislead their fellow town councillors, or hide things from them; Members of Parliament should not mislead the public; Members of Parliament should not mislead Parliament; Members of Parliament should not mislead the Court; Members of Parliament should not let their friends make money at the public's expense; and Members of Parliament should always act with integrity; and with candour and transparency.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am moving this Motion because integrity is of the utmost importance in elected officials.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singapore has succeeded only because we have maintained a culture of honesty and integrity in the Public Service.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Those who participate in politics must be honest, upright people who can be trusted to uphold the public interest, speak the truth even at a cost to themselves and admit their mistakes when they have done wrong.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have to uphold these principles even when it is politically inconvenient to do so.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And we need to do this, whether you are a Government or Opposition Member of Parliament, whether you represent a constituency in Parliament, or are a Non-Constituency Member of Parliament or Nominated Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Because if we cannot trust a politician to tell the truth, we cannot trust him to safeguard public funds, to put the public interest ahead of personal gain, or to make decisions in the best interests of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For this reason, we have always taken any accusations of dishonesty against political leaders very seriously.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Certainly, the fourth generation (4G) People's Action Party (PAP) leaders intend to continue maintaining the high standards which we have achieved and upheld for so many years since the PAP first formed the Government in 1959.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For we must ensure that Members of Parliament, both Government and Opposition, are men and women of integrity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is in the vital interest of Singapore and Singaporeans for Members of the Opposition also to be persons of integrity, and not people who cannot be trusted with public funds, much less national responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I might add, Mr Speaker, that we have had such upright, honourable men among the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I might mention Mr David Marshall, Mr AP Rajah and Mr Chiam See Tong.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If I might be permitted another personal note, Mr Low Thia Khiang ran his own Town Council well when he was Member of Parliament for Hougang.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Each of our Prime Ministers – Mr Lee Kuan Yew, Mr Goh Chok Tong and our current Prime Minister – has espoused and upheld the values of honesty, transparency and integrity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Each made integrity, honesty and incorruptibility fundamental values in Government.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If any PAP Minister or Member of Parliament is accused of lying, the Prime Minister would do a thorough investigation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And if they were found dishonest, serious consequences would inevitably follow.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Imagine if a Court had made such findings against PAP town councillors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Is it even conceivable that a PAP Member of Parliament whom the Court has described in these terms can remain in the Town Council and continue handling public funds as if nothing had happened?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the very least, he would have been asked to go on leave, pending any effort to clear his name through an Appeal.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What sort of questions would the Workers Party be asking the PAP?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What sort of demands would they be making of the Government?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Opposition must hold themselves to the same standards that they rightly apply to the Government.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is, in fact, precisely why we have our system of Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is an important way Singaporeans can judge for themselves who deserves to be given the responsibility to run the country, whether it is a Government Member of Parliament or an Opposition Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It allows them to identify which Members of Parliament and which political parties, can walk the talk, manage public monies and show that they can actually get things done.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Town Councils allow political parties to prove their mettle even if they are not the Government.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If a party can manage a Town Council well, it proves its competence to conduct good, clean, administration.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And their leaders can show that they are credible and deserve to be entrusted with broader responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If not, it is just as well that everybody finds out early, before too much damage is done.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Indeed, as I just noted, Mr Low Thia Khiang himself won his spurs when he was the Member of Parliament for Hougang and ran its Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Similarly, Mr Chiam See Tong in running Potong Pasir's Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, when the Workers' Party argues against the Town Council system instead of putting right their lapses, what does it mean?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Do they think the Opposition only exists to poke holes in Government policy, bandy around the slogan of "First World Parliament" but shoulder no other responsibility for residents?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Do they think Opposition Members of Parliament should not be held to the same standard as Government Members of Parliament, even though at each election, we are asking the same thing of voters – their trust?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Surely, this is not the sort of Opposition that Singaporeans need.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party cannot stay silent on this.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have not accounted for their dishonesties and untruths.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Nor have they have said whether they intend to put right the many wrongs that the Court has uncovered, and, if so, how.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is not the way to conduct yourself in politics.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Trust between the electorate and elected officials is vital in democratic societies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When trust breaks down, the people will feel that their leaders are disconnected and only seem to be looking after themselves and their friends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must never let this happen in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: (In Mandarin):   I move this Motion today because, for elected officials, integrity is of the utmost importance.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This saga has been going on for eight years, involving millions of dollars in public funds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Audit reports from AGO, KPMG and PwC, the suit brought to the Court by the independent panel appointed by AHTC itself, and the Court hearings, have all shown that these two Members of Parliament have committed wrongdoings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At numerous points over the last eight years, they could have admitted their wrongdoings and acted.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On the contrary, they either repeatedly camouflaged their wrongdoings, misled the public or remained silent, hoping that everyone will forget their wrongdoings over time.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Workers' Party won the Aljunied GRC at the 2011 General Election.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is understandable that they wanted to appoint a company that they can trust to manage the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: However, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang did not follow the proper procedures.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For example, they should have called an open tender, assessed all the bids and recorded the reasons for appointing FMSS in the minutes of the Town Council meetings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the process, FMSS had made huge profits.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What is even more worrying is that, when they were exposed, they were not willing to bear the responsibility for their actions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Instead, they continued to confuse people, made things difficult for the auditors, and misled the Courts, Parliament, residents and even the public.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Nearly four weeks have passed since the Court’s judgment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have let their residents of Aljunied and Hougang down.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have not asked Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves from dealing with financial matters of the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If the Workers' Party continues to remain silent and do nothing, we will be forced to conclude that the Workers' Party endorses the dishonest conduct and the breach of the fiduciary duties that has already occurred.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I hope that the Workers' Party will do the right thing and correct the financial and governance lapses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Sometimes, a bitter pill has to be taken to solve the root of the problems.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If the Workers' Party wants the privilege of representing Singaporeans, they cannot remain silent now.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The integrity of elected officials is of the utmost importance to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singapore's system of governance is based on integrity and accountability.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Those who participate in politics must be honest and upright in order to win the trust of the people and serve them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They should admit their mistakes when they have done wrong and correct them, even at a cost to themselves.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In many countries, the lack of integrity in politicians has become a norm.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If the politician cannot be trusted, it will be difficult for him to build a relationship of mutual trust with the public.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If the public do not trust him, they will not believe that he can put public interest ahead of personal gains and make the best decisions in the interest of the people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since Independence, our political and Public Service leaders have always upheld the fundamental value and principle of integrity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As a result, Singapore is able to make continuous progress and succeed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will continue to be important for Singapore’s future.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Whether you are a Government Member of Parliament, an Opposition Member of Parliament, a Non-Constituency Member of Parliament or Nominated Member of Parliament, you must agree that integrity is our core value.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have to ensure that the 4G leaders uphold a system of incorruptibility and integrity, and to maintain high standards which we have achieved since the PAP formed the Government.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If a PAP Member of Parliament makes a mistake, the Prime Minister would do a thorough investigation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Ms Sylvia Lim is a lawyer, but she has committed these wrongdoings knowingly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: He has managed the Hougang Town Council well for over 20 years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I always had a high regard of him.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, it pains me when I saw the Court's judgment on Mr Low Thia Khiang.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, to sum up what this Motion is about, it is about integrity and character expected of public officials and Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In politics, we must uphold the fundamental values of integrity, honesty and incorruptibility.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We know the words of the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They claim to stand for transparency and accountability.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But now, after eight long years, we know that their deeds show the contrary.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They appointed their friends to manage the Town Council at the higher cost than the previous MA.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They concealed the real facts and manipulated the circumstances of this appointment, even to the extent of misleading their fellow town councillors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They then told the public, their auditors and Parliament untruths about these circumstances.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They refused to give auditors documents, documents that might have shed light on their wrongdoing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even after these facts were uncovered by independent auditors, they took no action.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It took the Independent Panel that they appointed to finally bring them to Court to set things straight.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And even before the Court, they continued to perpetuate untruths.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even after all this has been made public, the Workers' Party has stayed silent.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Maybe they hope that Singaporeans will forget or forgive them.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Playing the victim or the underdog may be par for the course in politics, but there are important matters at stake – public funds, residents’ monies, the estates that Singaporeans come home to.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Given the Court’s findings, this is the least that they can do.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, it falls on all Members of this House to ask the Workers' Party what it intends to do, to put its own house in order.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first clarification is: in his speech, he mentioned that millions have been lost, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My question to him is: is this a finding of the Court?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does he not know that our consistent position has been that we owe statutory duties under the Town Councils Act?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Related to that, is he aware that this judgment of the High Court actually makes new law?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: If he looks at the summary from paragraph 6 onwards that he handed out to the House just now, the Court actually goes into explaining why it is actually making a finding that fiduciary duties apply in the context of Town Councils which has never been the settled law.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The third clarification is, he seemed to suggest that we had obstructed the AGO in its work.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I hope that he can clarify that because I do not think that the AGO actually said anything of that nature.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Fourth, he kept repeating that we had hidden documents from auditors which, if produced, would have revealed the truth.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Can he explain what exactly he is talking about?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I do not know what he was referring to.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The findings have been very clear in two auditors' reports and in the Court findings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: No, I did not say that millions had been lost.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: No, in fact, the High Court judgment, and you are a lawyer, you have read the High Court judgment carefully.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The High Court spent a lot of time looking at the question of what duties you owed – fiduciary duties that the town councillors owed to the Town Council, and the judgment was very clear on this point.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On the AGO's nature, you said, well, in what way did you not reveal documents to the AGO?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The fact is that there were many documents that were asked for, but the Town Council did not provide.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Despite that, the AGO had important findings that merited actions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, there were documents which were asked for, which you did not provide.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Fourth and finally, you asked about the auditors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Can I clarify what you asked about the auditors again?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Yes, Mr Speaker, what I had asked was, I think Deputy Prime Minister Mr Heng mentioned repeatedly that we had apparently hidden documents from auditors which, if produced, would have revealed the truth.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I believed this phrase came out more than once.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, may I ask what he is referring to?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Do you not recall emails for which you had said that you had asked Ms How Weng Fan to hide the truth on their appointment?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the end of it, while you argued about the Town Council system, you have earlier on in Parliament said that, in electioneering, you have talked about how the Town Council system disadvantaged Opposition parties.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Just now, he said that when we co-sign cheques, he seemed to imply that one can encash a cheque with just one signatory under AHTC.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: He said that what we said that cheques had to be co-signed either by the Chairman or either one of the Vice Chairmen is not the truth.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, is the Deputy Prime Minister implying that cheques can be encashed with just one signature even though we set it up as two signatures must be there before we can encash the cheque under AHTC?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Well, the Workers' Party Members have asked a whole series of questions on details.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But, let me get back to why I moved this Motion.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I moved this Motion because this is a question of integrity.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is a question of the way that we deal honestly in Parliament, with our residents, with the public and with our fellow town councillors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have asked very serious questions about how the transactions were done.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have asked questions of Mr Faisal Manap as to what he as Chairman of the Town Council would do.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have asked Mr Pritam Singh, as Secretary-General of the party and Ms Sylvia Lim as Chairman of the party, what you intend to do, given these serious findings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You have an interest to ensure that our system of governance in Singapore remains upright, that we have integrity in the system that elected Members of Parliament must be honest and upright in their dealings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But instead, you have asked me a whole range of other questions about whether it is one signature or two signatures.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Yes, but you see, the main question that I have asked is: the findings are that even on the question of signature of cheques, Ms Sylvia Lim has admitted that you have not gone through every transaction.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I am just asking you to stick to the main point and not detract.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I do not think that this is what we should be debating in this House – whether it is this path or that path – when the main issue that you ought to answer has not been answered.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The PAP Government is clearly excited about certain findings and comments contained in the High Court judgment issued on 11 October 2019.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: These are findings in relation to certain actions taken by some of us in the aftermath of the 2011 General Election.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: However, as the Deputy Prime Minister himself pointed out, Singapore has a Court structure that subjects High Court judgments to possible appeal to the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This avenue of appeal enables parties who are aggrieved by judgments of the High Court to seek review of the findings by the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Court of Appeal, consisting of at least three Judges of Appeal, will review the findings at the trial and may affirm, revise or vary the findings.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: If I might quote from the Supreme Court of Judicature Act, it is stated that "the Court of Appeal may draw inferences of facts and give any judgment and make any order which ought to have been given or made, and make such further or other orders as the case requires".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Under the applicable procedures, any party who is dissatisfied with the judgment can file a notice of appeal within one month.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In this case, the deadline for filing the appeal is 11 November, which is next Monday.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Whatever the trial judge has decided is subject to review by the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: This is a civil proceeding and involves novel points of law.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And contrary to what I think the Deputy Prime Minister had suggested, it has not been decided as to whether any loss has been caused to the Town Council.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And on this point, I should put this in perspective by referring to the summary which Deputy Prime Minister Heng distributed earlier – Annex 1, paragraph 27 – where the Judge states or it is summarised quite clearly that the legal burden of proving this falls upon the plaintiff.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, this point has not been decided as to whether loss has been proven.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: We are still pursuing the matter through the Courts and we thank everyone who has stood by us and helped us in our quest for justice.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We are proceeding with the Motion as planned.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I would like an adjournment for us to consider the matter and respond to her.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I will suspend the Sitting for 10 minutes.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You can do your consultations as you need to and then we will return.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.22 pm until 4.32 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Sun Xueling, would you like to speak?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Or is it Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The exact words that I have used are, "There are important questions of public interest to consider.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I would just mention a few at the outset.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Millions of dollars in public funds are involved." Those are the exact words that I have used.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I would also like to have two technical clarifications which were raised by Mr Png Eng Huat.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will ask the Member Mr Edwin Tong to take the two questions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The four disclaimers arose on the basis of incomplete documentation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They sought documents in relation to transactions that were entered into after the Workers' Party took over the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And the basis of the majority of those 13 disclaimers rested on the basis that incomplete documentation, absence of information, and they were unable, as a result, to verify the accounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When the AGO took over the matter, they also came across difficulties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: PwC, in particular, Ms Sylvia Lim will remember, were appointed to audit the accounts on behalf of the AGO.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Yes, I am reminded that those documents were eventually produced in Court.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I would like to draw your attention to the Court's judgment, which I am in no doubt you are familiar with, where the Court said it was substantially assisted by the voluminous amount of internal emails and correspondence, which he used to reach findings which we have heard the Deputy Prime Minister articulate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On Mr Png Eng Huat's comment on the cheques, I think the position is very clear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is not about one signatory or two signatories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is about the entire system that you have set up as a result of what you have done – by putting FMSS as your MA, the General Manager and the Secretary in the Town Council being owners of FMSS, that entire system has been completely subverted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A proper system has been subverted by the way in which you have done this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: You just have to look at the summary of the judgment to know that we are not talking about one cheque here or two signatories there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat would know this very well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Standing Instruction for payments to FMSS to be co-signed by the AHTC Chairman or Vice Chairman was not a sufficient safeguard because there was no system, no system, to ensure that each cheque presented was fully verified by the independent parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In some instances, there was no proper verification even by the conflicting parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, Mr Png well knows that we are not talking about one cheque here or two cheques there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The entire system on which you have sought to make payments to FMSS.

text: Two clarifications on what Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong had just said.

text: In relation to my query on whether we have ever been accused of hiding things from our own auditors, if I heard correctly, he basically was saying that the auditors had said that they had requested for certain documents which were not produced.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I accept that we had poor record keeping.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And I think the difference would be clear to most reasonable people.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second point is, if I heard him correctly, he was talking about the work done by PwC in 2017.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: He would recall, because I think he was the lawyer acting for them at the time, if I remember correctly, that they were actually appointed by PRPTC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: There was a question as to their Terms of Reference.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: They were told not to duplicate the work of KPMG and what they were asking was in relation to things that had happened before Punggol East even came under our charge.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If Ms Sylvia Lim wants to go into KPMG, then, let us go into KPMG.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When KPMG was appointed, I think Ms Sylvia Lim will remember that there was a media release that was given.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Not just one or two, but several documents and several email archives of persons belonging to AHTC and FMSS were removed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, KPMG sought the cooperation of town councillors when they came in to do the audit.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, when we say information and documents are missing and the auditors are unable to verify information, that is what we refer to – a litany of these excuses, documents are missing, cannot find the documents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Or as you say, not providing documents to an auditor when they ask for it, is not the same thing as hiding it, then I do not know what is.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because they asked once in 2011; second time in 2012.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Your own auditors Foo Kon Tan, AGO, PwC – PwC was appointed on behalf of AGO as well, initially – and then, now, KPMG.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, that is what we refer to, Ms Lim.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And finally, when you had to produce it in Court, we know what the Court has made of those emails and internal correspondence.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I just want to clarify that when the Senior Minister of State said about accounts being deleted from our computers, I think —

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: KPMG did the forensics; they actually did a deep-dive and a lot of undeleting.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: We helped them to uncover some of the lost emails as well.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: If there is anything wrong with the email, we were very transparent.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: We explained why some of the hard disk were recycled.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And some of the things were tagged wrongly as well, and we had to explain to them, if you go into the report, you can refer to KPMG.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: One other thing is that the Senior Minister of State kept referring to our auditors finding four points.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I hope the Senior Minister of State is aware that Foo Kon Tan was caught lying in the two reports about the opening balance.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The October 2016 report by KPMG records very clearly and I just gave two examples.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I invite Mr Png to look at it carefully.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It sets out the different employees whose emails had been missing, the archives are missing and it goes on to say that when they requested for the email profiles of certain persons, and when they received it, it goes on to say that they found out that those email profiles had just been accessed; and then, they said these were missing.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Yes, they do not say you took it, but I think there is an inference in there.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I invite you to look at it carefully.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It certainly does not say anything about AHTC assisting to replicate this file or that file, as you have explained.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked about details of how you have resisted disclosures.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Town Council, despite repeated requests, did not provide us with all the critical documents relating to these transactions" and "AHPETC did not provide us with all the necessary and relevant accounting documents and information which are essential and critical for our work." These came from your own auditors and the 2015 AGO report.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Auditor-General went to say, "Since the commencement of our review in April 2014, we have made various requests for documents from AHPETC as part of our review of selected transactions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In our view, these documents, such as documents which record the proper disclosure and consideration of related party transactions (RPTs) ought to exist as a matter of record.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Notwithstanding numerous requests and reminders, AHPETC did not provide a number of the requested documents." In the 2017 PwC report, and I quote, "Despite repeated requests, no correspondence and/or written correspondence, including, importantly, emails in relation to amongst others, the takeover of the MA and the EMSU services by FMSS, including the termination of CPG, the award of contracts to FMSS and all FMSS performance of works, were given to us.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: No single email was given to us for our review, although in our view, such emails ought to exist." So, Mr Png, I hope that you, as one of the town councillors, take your duties seriously and you have gone through all these.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am a little confused because Mr Pritam Singh says, "Let us continue the debate." Ms Sylvia Lim pointed out that it was premature.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: My objection is that the judgment is being appealed to the Court of Appeal and the Court of Appeal may reverse the findings or review and vary the findings of the High Court.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, it is premature for the Deputy Prime Minister to file this Motion to call upon the House to do anything when the findings are subject to review.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You confirm that this matter is not sub judice, right, in your view?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Do you confirm that this matter is not sub judice, in your view?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have not taken a position on sub judice.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It all depends on how the debate turns.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I want to remind the Members of this House, when I spoke about the Motion, I said that this Motion is about what is to be expected of Members of Parliament: integrity, honesty and being truthful in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, can I ask Ms Sylvia Lim: is this a proper subject for debate in this House?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If you wish to reply, Ms Sylvia Lim?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, the operative clause, of course, is the last one, where it calls upon AHTC to take certain actions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: That is the operative clause and I am just saying it is premature.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I said this Motion is about what is expected of Members of Parliament: integrity, honesty and being truthful in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There is a judgment of the High Court, which stands until the appeal is heard.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Members will know that when there are similar findings made in any corporate setting, it is only right and proper that those whose integrity has been impugned to step aside and recuse themselves until they clear their names.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I welcome the efforts of the Workers' Party Members of Parliament to clear their names but, until they do so, they have to be accountable to this House for the findings that the High Court has made.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: That must be doubly so when you are dealing with millions of dollars of public funds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I would like to ask the Town Council Chairman: what is your view on this matter?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You are the Chairman of your Town Council.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: (In Malay):   Sir, I do not support this Motion to ask AHTC to recuse Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim from the position or role of the Town Council which covers financial issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I have full confidence and trust in the integrity of Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe and trust that the actions and decisions taken previously when Ms Sylvia Lim led AHTC as its chairman and Mr Low Thia Khiang as its vice chairman when running AHTC, were made with the sincere intent to do their best for the residents of Aljunied-Hougang town.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: As Ms Sylvia Lim said earlier, she will be filing an appeal.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Hence, it is not appropriate to table and discuss this Motion.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So far, the Independent Panel has only issued a statement dated 11 October 2019, in which they acknowledged the judgment issued by the Court.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Nonetheless, I will present the Court’s judgment at the next Town Council meeting.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I am not sure Members of the Workers' Party appreciate it to the same extent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first limb, which affirms the vital importance of Members of Parliament maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability can brook no dissent.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Deputy Prime Minister has also outlined the Court's findings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are serious and grave findings, by any measure.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And Members of the Workers' Party who are lawyers and appear in Court will know that this is an exceptional judgment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is a serious and grave indictment of proper conduct and against various elected officials of the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They may say they disagree with the judgment – as I heard Ms Sylvia Lim said earlier – or that they wish to appeal, as I heard Mr Faisal Manap said a moment ago which, of course, you are entitled to do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the question is: what should happen in the interim?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think that is the measure of proper governance and probity that we are speaking about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Should those found to have engaged in egregious conduct recuse themselves from financial oversight and control?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To answer that question, we should consider what the Court found.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are the findings, until and unless they are set aside, and they are relevant for the interim period pending any appeal.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is a Court of law that has made a pronouncement after having heard Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim give evidence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This was not a one-off or an occasional lapse or one that was caused by lack of experience or by some careless oversight.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And on Mr Faisal Manap's point, that is not good faith.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They put their interests in wanting FMSS appointed ahead of the residents' interests.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When questions were first asked, starting from simple questions from the Town Council's own auditors – these are your own auditors looking at your accounts to try and understand if they are true and fair – came up with roadblocks, unable to obtain the documents; not once, not twice, but repeatedly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When questions arose as to why there was even a need to waive tender, they proceeded to offer a litany of false excuses to justify why FMSS had to be appointed without a tender.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: None of these excuses, which really kept shifting and changing, can stand up to scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But let me go back to the Town Council's accounts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First year, after the Workers' Party had taken over the Town Council in 2011/2012 and the accounts were being audited, your own town councillors, Foo Kon Tan Grant Thornton asked the Workers' Party in 2012 for financial information in respect of the period immediately following their takeover so that they could perform a proper audit on the Town Council’s accounts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Png Eng Huat would appreciate that that is usual, par for the course – they check, you answer, they verify and then, if it is true and fair, they sign off.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The simple and honest way of dealing with queries from your own auditor is to address them squarely, directly and fully and to provide the relevant documentation so that the appropriate review can be undertaken.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Town Council, at that time under Ms Sylvia Lim's chairmanship, however, refused.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The auditors had to make disclaimers, as I have said earlier, and that, we all know, is a very serious adverse outcome.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the same time, these were not complicated requests.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They were requests for the Town Council’s own documents – your own documents – concerning transactions that you entered into after taking over the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In response to reminders, AHPETC indicated that it could not locate some of the documents and was still looking for others, three months after the request for documents." In the first year of audit, it was not even a full year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The transactions that they were talking about in respect of which documents were sought could not be found at that stage, but suddenly surfaced when the Court looked at it?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I ask Ms Sylvia Lim to reconsider not providing the documents to Foo Kon Tan Grant Thornton when they asked – is it not the same as suppressing, prevaricating, not cooperating with the auditors?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it would not be lost on this House that the apparently missing documents are in respect of the period of time in which FMSS was appointed without a tender – the same relevant period.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It gets worse because this same charade was repeated the following year.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At that time, Foo Kon Tan Grant Thornton were performing an audit for the FY2012/2013, the first full financial year under the management of the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As in the previous year, Foo Kon Tan Grant Thornton were stonewalled.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They reported that, "The Town Council had not made available to us details of the project management service fee paid to a related party.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Accordingly, we are unable to determine the completeness of the related party transactions." This is found in your own annual report, FY2012/2013, page 14.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Foo Kon Tan were very specific and zeroed in on the appointment, and the payment terms, of FMSS which by that time they knew was a related party.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Why was this not made available to Foo Kon Tan?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Why did you not make it available to Foo Kon Tan?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Later on, when AGO and PwC were appointed to audit the Town Council's same accounts, 2012/2013 and look into the financial affairs of the Town Council, they had similar difficulties.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, why did you not produce those to the auditors, twice, to AGO, to PwC?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because, as I said, we knew from the Court judgment that the Court looked at voluminous contemporaneous documents in that critical period of time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Those were the same documents requested by PwC in assessing the reasons for the transactions and, of course, their propriety.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We then get to the stage where KPMG gets appointed and you heard what I said earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: AHTC took the position, "Let's not duplicate work, let's focus on cooperating only with KPMG", issued a media release – I read it out earlier – but then had a series of problems with KPMG, all documented in the report that I referred Mr Png Eng Huat to earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, what we see, Mr Speaker, is a clear, consistent pattern of behaviour.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not "I took over and maybe I was disorganised at the start." But it started in 2011 and right through to 2017.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And you clearly did not want to do that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, you carefully suppressed them, held them back from disclosure, fobbed off the request until you could no longer do so and it came out in the wash in the Court proceedings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Throughout the whole inquiry into this issue, for years, the Workers' Party said they provided all the information.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think that is being the consistent pattern in the media statements, in the letters written to the auditors and also in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, in February 2017, in a response to PwC, the Town Council said, and I quote, “we have provided all information relating to   request”.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I think the facts speak for themselves and PwC's subsequent report makes it quite clear.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I read a paragraph earlier from the April 2017 Report, six years after FMSS' appointment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They asked for documents in relation to the premature release of CPG, "This must have been the subject of correspondence between CPG and the Town Council and/or email discussions amongst or involving the town councillors" – not produced.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And again, on FMSS, PwC stated and asked, "Town Council met on 4 August 2011 to decide on the waiver of tender and FMSS' appointment as MA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Prior to this meeting, there must have been correspondence and/or email discussions amongst and/or involving town councillors concerning such waiver of tender and/or award of the first MA contract to FMSS.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These would shed light on the circumstances surrounding the waiver of tender and the award of the contract".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
