text: So, let me shift now to what these documents, in fact, show, when they were produced in Court, against the different versions, shifting versions proffered by Workers' Party to cover up the true picture.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Workers' Party first sought to justify the appointment of FMSS without tender as being critical and urgent because CPG, the then MA, wanted out, and this left AHPETC at that time exposed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This was a narrative that was repeated and played out consistently over several years.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There was no mistaking the picture that the Workers' Party wanted people to believe.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was CPG's fault, they left the Workers' Party in a lurch, without any MA, something which the Workers' Party only knew at short notice and, therefore, the appointment of FMSS was urgent, pressing and we had to waive tender.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These reasons were used to justify not calling a tender which you know, clearly, you are required to do by law.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And then, they put out this same picture in different fora as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But such a narrative was entirely false, one that was designed to give cover to the advancement of their own collateral motives, whilst at the same time sacrificing the interests of residents.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang knew there was no urgency.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Court heard from both of you, Mr Low and Ms Lim, and came to this conclusion, after having heard you.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CPG was required in law to continue as the MA.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They could not walk away as the MA even if they wanted to.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Neither could they not offer you the prevailing rates that they had been using and charging the previous Town Council.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They were committed to it but you were not.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: CPG's position was inconvenient to both Ms Lim and Mr Low, since you wanted FMSS appointed, whatever the case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And to get FMSS in, you had to make it look as if CPG wanted out.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it is very apparent from the evidence you gave in Court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim's evidence in Court under oath was that she did not even ask to see the CPG’s contract.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: She did not know what the terms were, did not know the termination mechanisms were, did not know what the contractual rights might have been.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, far from seeking to protect their resident's interests in the face of sudden unanticipated circumstances – a narrative which the Workers' Party had very painstakingly spun, the Judge found that they had, in fact, painted a misleading picture to the world, leading everyone to believe that they were compelled to appoint FMSS without any tender and masking the fact that they did not act in the best interests of the Town Council and of the residents it serves.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Judge did not mince his words on this sorry episode.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He called it, at various occasions, "misleading", "not honest", the picture was "not a truthful one", "camouflaged" and "not the true picture".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But he was particularly galled by how such a misleading narrative was conveyed to the public, and specifically to the very constituents which the elected Members of Parliament were elected to serve in the first place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, a misleading narrative, repeatedly put out over several years, to the public, in Parliament, in Court, by Members of Parliament who knew perfectly well this narrative was not true.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Another contrived excuse for the set up of FMSS was that it was only a contingency, just in case.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On 13 May 2013, Ms Sylvia Lim told this House, and I quote, "The set-up of FMSS was because of this very real possibility that we will be faced with nobody else to do it for us." This, again, is a wholly untenable position to take.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Workers' Party was clear and deliberate in themselves not wanting CPG to carry on.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, what contingency are we even talking about?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Judge's finding that I have outlined above completely demolishes any notion that FMSS was meant as a contingency.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was, in fact, premeditated and a fait accompli.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Another excuse that has been constantly trotted out by the Workers' Party, in an attempt to justify the waiver of tender, you use the fact that AIM had terminated the TCMS.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This House will know, Mr Speaker, that this has been used before, to give off the impression that, this time, it is AIM, a PAP vehicle, which had forced AHTC to hurriedly appoint FMSS without a tender.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim will also recall that in an election rally on 2 September 2015, the blame was put squarely on this termination as being the reason for the Town Council not having called a tender for the appointment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It might well have been a convenient election rhetoric, but as her own evidence in Court has revealed, it was also an entirely false excuse.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The truth is that there was no question of the termination having played any part in necessitating a waiver of tender.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Indeed, Ms Sylvia Lim will recall that when you were shown contemporaneous documents in Court, you accepted to the Court that AIM had, in fact, had been helpful to your Town Council – helpful – that AIM was assisting in circumstances beyond what they were required to do; and that AIM gave more time to AHTC than it was required to do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim will remember this very clearly.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, at trial, Ms How Weng Fan also disclosed a conversation, where she said it was actually Ms Sylvia Lim, and I quote, who "doesn't want to extend" AIM.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, what we see with the disclosure of documents and when matters had gone to Court are a very different picture from what we have heard, a very different picture from what Ms Sylvia Lim has sought to be put out in the press, in Parliament and, of course, at election rallies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, Mr Speaker, what we see, looking back over the years at this long and very sorry saga, is the Workers' Party shifting from one untenable excuse to another, in order to justify appointing FMSS without calling a tender.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And this itself is set against a backdrop of constantly refusing to disclose to auditors, your own as well as those from AGO and KPMG, fobbing off inquiry at every turn, refusing to do interviews so that the real reason could remain suppressed until, as we see, their own Independent Panel decided to bring this action and it unravelled in Court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, let me round up by going back on what this Motion calls on the Workers' Party to do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang continue today as elected councillors, including having financial oversight over the affairs of the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Surely, this status quo cannot continue, given what the Court has found.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said at the start, the conduct in respect of which the Court has found was not caused by a one-off occasional or even careless error.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was calculated, careful, deliberate, an outcome that was obtained by much planning, design and engineering.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The elected councillors continue today to be in AHTC, to continue today to run the Town Council and that includes having control and oversight over financial matters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, on this, two points stand out for me.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is already astonishing enough for an elected official to ask for a report to be sanitised so that it passes the auditors' eyes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We all know what "pass the auditors' eyes" means.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If it was a truthful report, and you knew it to be truthful, there should be nothing that needs to be done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, clearly, this was not the case here.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But to add insult to injury, this sanitising was to be done by the very persons whose appointment without tender the report itself was meant to recommend – How Weng Fan and Danny Loh.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Even a child knows that you do not ask the fox to guard the chicken coop, or a wolf to watch the sheep.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But this little episode provides an insight into the way in which affairs are being conducted at AHTC.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And Ms Sylvia Lim continues in a position of having financial oversight over matters today.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: How can this status quo be allowed to continue?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Whatever your views are on the judgment, today, this judgment represents the position in law.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Until it is set aside, this judgment is valid.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second point which stood out for me was the way in which the councillors, your councillors, who are supposed to be the check and the approving authority with independent judgment, were instead completely sidelined, misled and effectively made use of.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Councillors are charged with the responsibility to make decisions about the town they manage, and often, there are significant financial repercussions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this case, at crucial Town Council meetings, the Court found – and, again, let me quote – that there had been "a palpable economy of truth in the way things were disclosed" at Town Council meetings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In particular, the decision to delegate authority to Ms Sylvia Lim to undertake matters on behalf of the Town Council was also obtained without proper disclosure of facts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To give this House a sense of what happened, two Town Council meetings concerning FMSS at the relevant time were called, one in June and another in August 2011.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Councillors were not told at the June 2011 meeting that a letter of intent, there was intent to be signed with FMSS in July 2011, even though, by that time, the Workers' Party had already decided to appoint FMSS.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the second Town Council meeting in August 2011, the councillors thought that they were going to a meeting to approve a waiver of tender in order to appoint FMSS, not knowing that FMSS had actually already been appointed, or that FMSS themselves had helped to sanitise the very report that made the recommendation about the waiver of tender over their appointment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In fact, your councillors were given a very misleading picture.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I said at the start, it is your right to appeal and seek to overturn the findings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But until then, in the interim, common decency and practice requires that they recuse yourselves from having oversight of financial matters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we call on the Workers' Party to abide by their own single thread – and Mr Pritam Singh knows this well – of transparency and accountability, and to put residents’ interests first.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the speech that Mr Faisal Manap made, let me ask a few questions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, the Member said it is not appropriate to consider the Motion at this time.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are talking about what is to happen in the interim in the Town Council, over which you are the Chairman, until you get the reversal from the Court of Appeal, if that happens.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, can Mr Faisal Manap explain in the interim why is it not appropriate to be talking about actions that you should take now to safeguard, to ensure that your residents' interests come first?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If, for example, a teacher was found to have done something wrong – a teacher who interacts with students every day – then he cannot teach until he clears his name on an appeal.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I have to take into consideration the mandate given by Aljunied residents at General Election 2015, amidst the AHTC saga, where the residents of Aljunied had decided to still give mandate to Mr Low Thia Khiang, Ms Sylvia Lim and the other three of us to manage their town.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Personally, it will be improper for me to cancel this mandate.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I take the mandate given to us, the Workers' Party's Members of Parliament, seriously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because these are the very same issues that the Court in this case has made very serious and egregious pronouncements.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, in relation to the suggestion that the mandate was given in 2015, but today we are in 2019, and the judgment has been released after having heard all parties, and certain findings have been made.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: But it is subject to an appeal, as mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   	Mr Speaker, the Motion moved by Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat in Parliament just now is an important one because it involves the conduct and actions by Members of Parliament who are also Workers' Party leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This Motion draws our attention to the key issue, that is, the question of integrity and honesty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: By doing nothing and letting the AHTC case be left at that, we, as Members of this Chamber, will be seen as neglecting our duty.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Is it appropriate for us to stay silent?

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Judge said that their actions of awarding a contract without calling a tender and painting a misleading picture about the appointment of FMSS, showed that they did not act in the interest of AHTC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Court also said that, as experienced town councillors, Mr Low Thia Khiang should have known that a tender is required for that appointment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The AHTC case has gone on for so long until it has reached the Courts, and those involved were given the room and opportunity to defend their actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Therefore, what is the right thing that they should do, and what should be the right action taken by the Workers' Party leadership?

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And what should all of us in this Chamber do as our responsibility to the people and our residents?

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The key point that we need to know is what kind of appropriate action that should be taken if there is a lack of integrity, because without integrity, our institutions will weaken.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every individual, whether they are leaders, representatives of the people, or organisation and corporate heads, must display integrity, because it is an important characteristic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Integrity is an important pillar of good governance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The management of the Town Council in providing services to its residents, must surely place importance on integrity and transparency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: AHTC must not neglect this obligation, what more by acting dishonestly towards the residents of Aljunied and Hougang.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Those responsible must be taken to task and take responsibility when there is any wrongdoing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Town Councils were formed in 1989 with the function and responsibility of managing and maintaining public housing estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, it is unavoidable for Town Councils to have a political element because there is a political competition for the right to administer a Town Council.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In this context, the residents of Aljunied and Hougang should rightly feel disappointed when High Court Judge Kannan Ramesh said that it was unsatisfactory that the narrative conveyed by those involved in the case was misleading the public, especially the residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is clear that their action of not calling a tender appears to be due to other intents and considerations, including political considerations, said the Judge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Therefore, it is the Government’s responsibility to correct this situation in order to protect the interest of the people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, we are faced with this important Motion that aims to safeguard our high standards of integrity and commitment as Members of this Chamber.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Protecting this integrity will enable us to perform our duties responsibly to our residents whom we represent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Otherwise, it will weaken our institutions to the point that we will lose the people's trust.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our integrity is one of the key reasons that help us get elected and is one of the main factors that differentiates our public office from other countries’ systems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Although we want the justice system to proceed smoothly, unfortunately, many facts revealed in the Court's judgment raised a lot of concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The people's interest supersedes other interests, including political interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Although the management of Town Councils has a political element, this does not mean that political interests should be prioritised over administrative and financial responsibilities and obligations, as well as the people's interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We debate this Motion today with no intention to point out mistakes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What is important is the restoration of integrity and trust towards an organisation, and how AHTC can recover from this incident.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim, as people in a position of power and influence, are not the first ones to step out of line and conducted themselves badly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What is important is how they will be dealt with and how they will take responsibility for conduct that broke the rules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If the same thing happens anywhere else, including in the PAP Town Councils, community organisations or corporate sector, those responsible will surely recuse themselves from their duties until the process is complete.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It shows their level of integrity and sense of responsibility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope that AHTC will practise a high standard of governance in its service to the residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap, as the Chairman of AHTC, should be concerned over this issue.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, what are the steps that he will take to safeguard the integrity of AHTC’s management for the sake of their residents’ interests?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   	On 11 October, the High Court delivered a verdict on the AHTC case.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This was a disregard of the Town Council's interest, and a clear violation of its financial rules.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang even asked Ms How Weng Fan and Danny Loh to sanitise the reports to pass the audit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Other town councillors were also kept in the dark.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The judge pointed out that these behaviours were "not transparent", "dishonest", "egregious" and "unacceptable".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The AHTC saga has been going on for eight years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The problems were discovered together by various parties in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The financial issues of the Town Council were first discovered by auditors appointed by the Town Council itself.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2015, AGO assessed that AHTC's governance did not pass the bar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Town Council later appointed KPMG as an independent auditor who has found many improper payments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: After that, the Town Council appointed an Independent Panel to follow up on KPMG's report, and the Independent Panel advised that the Town Council sue three Members of Parliament of the Workers' Party.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang are still trying to find excuses at this juncture, I feel that it will make people more confused, and it is truly regrettable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The residents trust us and give us their votes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have a duty to take care of their needs, treat them with honesty and make sure that their interests are protected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must ensure the proper use of the residents' money and public funds.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In order to protect the residents' interest, the most important thing is to rely on an open and transparent system, such as an open tender, audit, legal processes, and Parliamentary debate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When things are in the dark, they get mouldy easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When things are open and transparent, mistakes will be easily discovered and corrected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: That is why everyone must follow the rules and due processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They should not try to make short cuts and evade oversight.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Workers' Party often talked about transparency, oversight and accountability in the past.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Yet, based on the evidence brought forth by various parties and the Court’s verdict, we see that some Members of Parliament of the Workers' Party are not at all open and transparent in handling their own Town Council affairs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: What is worse, they have even tried to cover up the truth, deceive other town councillors and ask other people to sanitise the report so that they can have a veneer of truth and integrity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This has severely violated what they themselves have once espoused.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: How should we look at what they have said before?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: How can we trust their promises in future?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Residents not only judge a Member of Parliament by his words, but also his actions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They not only look at the surface of things, but also the inside.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: On the surface, AHTC does not seem to have any problems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Yes, there are still people doing maintenance on the properties, elevators are still running, and the landscaping is still being done.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, the Members of Parliament have actually breached their fiduciary duties, caused conflict of interest, resulting in the mismanagement of the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Integrity is at the centre of all values and the foundation of Singapore's society and politics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Integrity is manifested through good governance, and is what differentiates Singapore from many other parts of the world in terms of public service and the Parliamentary system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Only with integrity can we accomplish the task of serving the people and each constituency.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If Members of Parliament lack integrity, the very foundation of Singapore's politics will be undermined, so will the confidence of people in our governance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When a Member of Parliament has done something illegal, whether he is not afraid to bear the responsibility or looking for excuses will be watched by everyone, including young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: When a Member of Parliament lacks integrity and that affects residents' interest, how should the Parliament react?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Should we just keep quiet on this matter, or look at it seriously and try to rectify?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our choice will also affect the political climate in Singapore and people’s trust in the Government.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It will also have a profound impact on young Singaporeans' thinking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Integrity and a healthy political climate are worth all of us to defend, because we care about Singapore's future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Earlier, I listened to Mr Faisal Manap and what he has said.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The right choice is often a very difficult one.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The right choice now is to recuse from all financial matters in the Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For Singapore's future, I hope that we can make the right choice.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As Members of this House may be aware, I was elected Member of Parliament for Potong Pasir in 2011.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As a result, I took over the management of the Potong Pasir Town Council from Mr Chiam See Tong of the Singapore People's Party (SPP) after 27 years.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: A transition was the first order of business.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This was quite similar to what transpired at Aljunied GRC in 2011 at about the same time.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It will be fraught with difficulties and problems.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I started serving in Potong Pasir in the year 2000, about 20 years ago.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: For 11 years, from 2000 to 2011, we fought a good, clean fight between Mr Chiam See Tong's team and ours.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It was a hard fight nevertheless and we worked very hard to win the hearts and minds of our residents.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We were happy but immediately understood the heavy responsibility and daunting task that lay before us.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I knew that for every two residents I met, one voted for us and one did not.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We are now in charge, but we are cognisant that we owe a duty of care and service to all Potong Pasir residents.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Because we understood, fundamentally, that we are in charge, our ultimate responsibility must be towards the well-being of all our residents.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The General Election was over; politics must now take a back seat.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I have great personal respect for Mr Chiam See Tong.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: He was a formidable opponent, but I knew he always puts our residents' interests first in whatever decision he makes.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: However, the transition then remained a difficult one when we took over the Town Council in 2011.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I remember a particular SPP member who frequented the Town Council office almost every day then to advise the staff to claim one month of compensation for every year of service if they were to lose their jobs.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I was informed some of the staff at the Town Council then had worked there for almost 27 years!

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The easy way out then would be for me to pay them the compensation they asked for.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We are only the custodians of the monies.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In addition, at that time, we also inherited a Town Council that already had severe financial challenges.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There was no way we could pay anyone any financial compensation.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We were well aware that most, if not all, of the staff then were supporters of the SPP.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We redeployed some of the staff to other Town Councils and retained some.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Today, two of these staff are still with us.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We were very clear in our minds we cannot let our residents down.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We had to get on with our task of building a better home and, really, there was no time for politics.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: One week after the 2011 General Elections, rubbish was piling up all over the estate.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We were told that the maintenance contractors appointed by the previous Town Council had stopped work for no good reason.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We had many problems to fix and we did.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: They patrolled our estate daily to ensure cleanliness and that essential services were functioning normally.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: At the same time, we also had to deal with situations, such as fairly large groups of petitioners seeking signatures to request for a by-election after the General Election.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There were scenes of great disappointment of SPP supporters at our coffee shops, post the General Election.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We had to level up and reunite the community.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It was a tough and stressful time for all of us then.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I pay tribute to our team in Potong Pasir.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: They were stoic and unwavering in the heat.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We came together with whatever we had to deliver our promise to the residents of Potong Pasir.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This even includes the financial situation of the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We visited these households, assisted them where required and put in place plans that were acceptable to their financial situation.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is the same in most corporate takeovers.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But the stakes in Town Councils are much higher because we are dealing with the lives and well-being of thousands of families.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We were clear in our minds that we had a heavy duty to discharge.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There were no celebration or sweeping changes made in Potong Pasir post-General Election 2011.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Teething issues abound and serving our residents and ensuring that their lives are not disrupted unnecessarily were at the top of our minds.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Pritam Singh, would you like to respond to any of the previous speakers?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Yes, Mr Speaker, if I may address Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong's intervention earlier on three points.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The first is, of course, he re-narrates the findings made by the trial Judge on certain matters in the aftermath of the 2011 General Elections on the circumstances of the departure of the former MA, on the impact of AIM and so on and so forth.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And he rightly points out, we have consistently maintained these circumstances were the circumstances that we had to deal with in the aftermath of the 2011 General Elections.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, this is something that we are going to appeal on and we will also highlight to the Judge certain evidences that may not have been given proper weight, including, for example, the termination notice issued to us by AIM.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, that is just to round off that first point.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I must admit that I feel a little bit like an interstitial break right now.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: First, I acknowledge the judgment delivered by the High Court on 11 October 2019.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Part (i) of the Motion which affirms the vital importance of Members of Parliament maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability is indisputable.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, I am also concerned that the Motion relates to matters which have not fully concluded in Court.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: A resolution of the House is not legislation, nor does it have any legal force.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Given this, should the call for AHTC to discharge their responsibilities as proposed in part (iv) of the Motion – asking for this House to call for and influence AHTC to recuse the said Members of Parliament "from all matters relating to, and oversight over, financial matters" – be made by the Minister through the powers granted by the Town Councils Act instead of this House?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, Mr Speaker, I am also uncomfortable with judgment being discussed in this House.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Given this, Mr Speaker, I am concerned that any comments that we make now, while possibly protected under certain Parliamentary privileges, could still potentially fall under contempt of Court.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Also, our debates are published in Hansard and the media.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I worry that commenting on and acting from the judgment when the case is not concluded with finality, especially if this matter is brought to the Court of Appeal, may be perceived to be interfering with the due judicial process in the administration of justice.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Given that this Motion shall be voted in its entirety and not in parts, I wish to state for the record that I clearly support the ideals of integrity and accountability expected of Members of this House in part (i).

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: This abstention does not in any way signal any disagreement on my part with the principles of integrity and accountability that we must uphold as Members of Parliament, elected or not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: There are two principles I am concerned with.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The first is affirming the high standard of behaviour expected of a Member of Parliament.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I agree with the Deputy Prime Minister that Members must maintain high standards of integrity and accountability.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I have read the judgment in this case.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The learned Judge finds that the circumstances, including the argued difficulty of working with the previous "PAP-affiliated MA", were an excuse and not a justification for waiver of tender.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But that said, I will stand corrected, but I have not seen evidence in the judgment that this breach was motivated by personal self-enrichment on the part of the hon Members.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This is not to excuse the breach of fiduciary duty.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But I have heard the hon Member Ms Sylvia Lim and noted their intention to appeal and I respect that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The second principle concerns Parliament's role in effectively addressing this serious breach of fiduciary duty for the benefit of residents and Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Part (iv) of this Motion calls on the Town Council to recuse Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang for financial matters.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: It is led by the elected Members of that Constituency.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This Motion essentially calls on the Workers' Party to undertake a certain course of action.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The Motion is not binding on the Town Council.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, I am personally concerned that this part of the Motion has the effect of a political resolution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I would have hoped that there were other means of addressing the serious concerns raised in this judgment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, I recognise that other Nominated Members are entitled to hold a different view.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: I know that integrity and good governance are paramount to this Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, Ms Anthea Ong makes good points about the importance of integrity and about the privilege placed being in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In effect, Ms Anthea Ong is suggesting that this matter is sub judice, a point which the Members of the Workers' Party have indicated, is not their position.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And I wonder why is it sub judice in effect, in her words when we are talking really about what ought to happen in the interim between findings of a High Court and such point in time when the appeal is heard and disposed of.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think that really is the crux of the matter and that really is why we are here today.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, we have a case, say, in a company.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Let us say directors of a company are sued by the company and found on similar terms, as the High Court has found in this case, to have been dishonest to have hidden facts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And the directors say, "Well, I will appeal.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will appeal the findings." Resolutely, want to appeal the findings.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But what happens in the interim, as a matter of proper corporate governance?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Quite apart from whether regulators come in or the company comes in and say we better go on garden leave or the rules require you to recuse yourself, quite apart from external regulatory action, what is that a fiduciary, a director, ought to do when there are findings of fact and law by the Supreme Court, pending an appeal by the director?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, I think that really is the narrow issue we are talking about, but it is an issue of great importance.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Say a person is, again, a fiduciary, head of a charitable organisation, say, a charitable foundation or one of our social service agencies or a voluntary welfare organisation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The person, again, is custodian of public funds, donors' funds, philanthropists' funds, and there is an allegation that this individual in charge of the charity, say, a director or a trustee, has mismanaged the funds.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And a suit has been taken by the charity or by the charity regulator against this trustee or fiduciary.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And a Court finding, no less a finding of the High Court, has been found that this trustee or fiduciary had, indeed, mismanaged – not just mismanaged by negligence or by carelessness but because of dishonesty.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Is the trustee and fiduciary going to carry on and say, "Carry on the next months or years until the findings are confirmed by the Appellate Court"?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: What should fiduciaries or people in that position do in the interim when findings have been found?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are not talking about before a suit is filed.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And Ms Anthea Ong makes a point about section 43(d) of the Town Councils Act.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I am familiar with that provision because I had to move those amendments in this very House to make sure that the regulators have the levers to act if we have to.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And section 43(d) comes after this saga has taken place in 2011.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: More importantly, the provision gives powers to the Minister after a report or compliance review has been undertaken under the Act as amended or after an investigation.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Be that as it may, ultimately, you have a judgment of the High Court by a Justice of the Supreme Court.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And I come to the last point that Ms Anthea Ong makes, which is, that she feels uncomfortable discussing this.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And, in a way, also Assoc Prof Walter Theseira's point about political resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I do not blame the two Nominated Members of Parliament or members of the public if they perceive this to have partisanship colours.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But actually, if you strip it down to its very core, what should fiduciaries do?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And, in this case, not any fiduciary, but one sitting amongst us held to certain standards by members of the public.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: What would our friends from the Workers' Party expect if there were such a finding, if it ever were to reach such a stage that the High Court finding were to be made of one of my colleagues or one of the Members of the ruling party in this House?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, what would we expect of ourselves, no less?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, I think we should be very clear that this is not about partisanship.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: What are you going to do in that interim period to assure the public that you are doing the right thing?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For the reasons I have articulated earlier, I do not think that that is the right thing to do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I do not think that is considered political.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: That, I think, is something that anyone in a company, anyone in an institution, anyone in the society, anyone in an organisation will do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And if they see us in this House not even doing that, then what do you think members of the public would think of the standards that we uphold here in this very House?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Is it lower than in some other organisation in Singapore but outside this House?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think we must all do the right thing.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And I also found it concerning that when asked directly, the Chairman of the Town Council says, "Well, I will not do anything in the meantime because, one, I have known the two members against whom the Judge had made findings of dishonesty since 2006.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, never mind what the High Court Judge says.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I will not act." Second, he says, "Well, I am the Chairman of Town Council, but the Independent Panel did not give me any advice, did not tell me what to do." No less the Chairman of the Town Council – waiting for the Independent Panel to tell the Chairman what is the right thing to do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And then, thirdly, after some time, he says, "Well, it is because the case is being appealed on".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I think it is very clear what the position of the Workers' Party is on what they plan to do or not do in the interim.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: How well we manage and run our Town Councils will reflect to the public, not just on our abilities but on what we stand for.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But MND recognises the political nature of Town Councils and accept that political considerations can, indeed, go into the appointment of contractors for Town Councils.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But such latitude must be exercised by town councillors within the boundaries of our laws.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And public funds and residents' interests must at all times be properly safeguarded.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, yes, Town Councils are creatures of politics.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It allows Members of Parliament to show politically to the public what they are able to achieve.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But certainly, at the very least, there are some boundaries, and those boundaries are laws and also boundaries of ethics and of integrity.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In other words, the Workers' Party wanted to appoint their friends.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They wanted to reward them for their loyalty over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But as I said earlier, there is a proper process and there are rules that govern even a creature of politics.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In particular, the Town Council rules provide for an open tender process and the Deputy Prime Minister has articulated very clearly how that comes into play.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But in this case, the Court found that the entire process had been deliberately subverted.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Right from the start, the Workers' Party Members of Parliament were clear that they did not want to work with the incumbent MA, CPG or any other MA in the industry.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The late Mr Danny Loh could confidently put up the capital as the MA contract was assured.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But to ensure that FMSS was appointed, the Workers' Party knew that CPG had to be removed from the picture and they did not want to call a tender.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And they wanted to hide this plan with a smoke screen.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The High Court found that "steps had to be taken to ensure that this did happen without the true motivations being unfounded." These steps include the following.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, as early as 13 May 2011, the elected Members instructed Ms How Weng Fan to write to CPG to arrange for the taking over of the management of the Town Council.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This was before the elected Members of Parliament met with CPG on 30 May 2011 and before CPG expressed any intention to be released from its contract.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, the High Court did not accept the point that any of this had to do with CPG's intention.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And the fact of the matter was that the Workers' Party Members of Parliament had proceeded after the 2011 General Election on "an independent and simple-minded course of action" to replace CPG.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They did not review the CPG contract to satisfy themselves whether CPG was entitled to prematurely terminate the contract before meeting with CPG on 30 May 2011.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, CPG was kept completely in the dark about FMSS.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Workers' Party Members of Parliament were concerned that if CPG was aware of the details behind the formation of FMSS, they would whistleblow and sound the alarm.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The High Court found that there was a consistent and concerted effort to keep the true facts away from CPG's eyes which included postponing their second Town Council meeting to discuss the waiver of tender until after CPG's departure.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And third, an excuse had to be given to the other town councillors to justify the waiver of tender.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A story was thus spun about the alleged urgency to appoint the new MA caused apparently by CPG's sudden announcement on 30 May that it intended to depart, the abrupt termination of the Town Council's system, the TCMS by AIM, and the lack of contractors who wanted to work for the Workers' Party.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But the fanning of this smokescreen was egregious because the case for urgency was completely manufactured.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, you see this is a deliberate matter.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, the report sought to "cloak the appointment of FMSS with a veneer of propriety" and to paper over the cracks.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In fact, as Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat and Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong had pointed out, it is deeply troubling that Ms	Sylvia Lim had asked Ms How Weng Fan and Mr Danny Loh, whose conflict of interest was crystal clear, to examine such report to see if it would "pass the auditor's eyes".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This serves to illustrate the lengths that the Workers' Party went to pull wool over the eyes of the other town councillors.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I say this to illustrate the key point that yes, there are civil cases and there are civil cases.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But look at what the Judge found in this particular civil case and ask ourselves whether, as fiduciaries or as town councillors, what is the right thing to do pending an appeal?

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is one thing to award contracts to friends for political reasons but another to allow them to reap a profit or to pay them more.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There appears to have been substantial double counting in the charging of fees and then when it came to the second MA contract, having only gained barely a year's experience in managing a GRC, it is astonishing that FMSS sought to put in even higher rates.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Workers' Party allowed them to do that.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The extent of such overcharging by FMSS remains to be determined by that process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In a short span of two years, the Town Council was run to the ground.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It bears noting that FMSS had one and only one client, which is AHTC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In other words, all profits came from the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On that point, I was also surprised when Ms Sylvia Lim mentioned earlier in this debate that this case involved a novel point of law, of fiduciary duty.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A town councillor elected by members, by electors, running a Town Council, a statutory entity, looking after public funds, has duties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But, in fact, in Court, their lawyers argued that there is nothing that anyone can do if monies were lost, except through the ballot box.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It would have been a different story, Sir, if they had ensured that their friends had charged fairly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Given the lack of track record and experience, there was simply no basis for FMSS to charge the same rates as CPG or more.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Workers' Party should have ensured that they charged less, especially in circumstances where no tender was called.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, this is to illustrate the seriousness of the findings and, therefore, why action should be taken in the interim to safeguard public resources until the appeal is heard.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The findings in the High Court judgment have now answered some of the key questions concerning FMSS that were raised by various accountants previously.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We now know the true story behind the FMSS saga, as clearly articulated by the High Court.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I come back to the core of today's Motion, which is: what is the Workers' Party going to do about this in the meantime?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If the same had happened in the corporate context, the management would recuse themselves from running the company.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In other Town Councils, errant officers step down.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The general manager of Ang Mo Kio Town Council had to step down and face the music.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: He was charged and pleaded guilty eventually to corruption charges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Let professionals or other Workers' Party Members of Parliament who are not implicated to manage the financial affairs and transactions of the Town Council until the appeal is disposed.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Before I go into my speech proper, I just wanted to clarify a few things with Ms Anthea Ong.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I was just trying to understand her position and hopefully be able to assist in clarifying some things.

speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Can I first check, does the hon Nominated Member of Parliament think that an appeal precludes discussion of this Motion?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: No, and actually I was about to clarify to Minister Desmond Lee's point in response.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: When I say I felt uncomfortable, I am talking about the fact that clearly as a non-legally trained person, I just feel uncomfortable that all these are being discussed so openly.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: And I am totally with Minister Desmond Lee's point.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I am not disputing there is a need for action, which is why I brought up another pathway for that action to be taken instead of this Motion in the House.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: My discomfort comes from us discussing so many details about the judgment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Given that I am not a lawyer, I was just uncomfortable.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: That could be potential interference or perceived to be interference, given that.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As I understand the position, Ms Anthea Ong is not saying that an appeal precludes a discussion of this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is just that feeling of discomfort with all the discussions going on.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That really brings me to what this Motion is about.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Is it about the facts and the Court judgment, or is it about something else?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Well, this Motion is about the standards of integrity and accountability to which Singaporean Members of Parliament are held, and that applies to all Members of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is about what do we regard as the appropriate standards for accountability, transparency and good governance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is not the finding of any of the Members here.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is a conclusion that the Court reached after looking into the matter in detail and seeing all the documents.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, you have a High Court judgment with these findings and the question now is this: what do you do in the interim period?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I appreciate that Ms Sylvia Lim has said that they will be filing an appeal, as, indeed, that is their right to do so.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the question is, between now and the time that the appeal is heard, what is the appropriate thing for a Member of Parliament to do?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What is the appropriate thing for a town councillor to do?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in response to Ms Anthea Ong, this is not sub judice because we are not making any suggestion that the findings were right or wrong.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In fact, what this Motion does is accept the findings as they are and it asks, between now and the time where it may or may not be reversed or upheld, what do you do?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Do you simply disregard what the judgment says, or do you say that, pending the appeal, and whilst there is a cloud hanging over the heads of these town councillors, do they stand down?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Do they wait, and then see what the Court of Appeal says?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Or do they say, "Well, in the meantime, it does not really matter if there is a judgment, I carry on as usual"?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is important because the Workers' Party's response to this important issue will tell you what are their values and what do they regard as good governance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Supposing you were to apply this attitude to this Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Supposing a Government official was found to have acted dishonestly and in breach of duty.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Let him or her remain in place, because he is appealing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It does not matter if it is a civil servant, if it is the Head of Civil Service, if it is the Commissioner of the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF)".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a finding of dishonesty, of lack of candour, lack of integrity.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Do we say, "Yes, it is okay, you can keep that person in place"?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under our rules of governance, it is equally important to ask what you do in the meantime, even if there is an appeal?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And very often, even before you get the first judgment, we will interdict.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: You do not allow the person to stay in place whilst there are issues hanging over that person.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: That is not what we are even asking here.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: How many times in this Parliament, when an incident has happened, have Members of Parliament stood up, calling for action against public officials?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Calling for action to be taken even before inquiries have been completed, even before judgment has been given?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Very often, interim measures are taken to make sure that not only is something properly done, but it is also seen to be done.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Members of Parliament are elected public figures, and so are Opposition Members of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the question is: what sort of governance do you hold to?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Why do the same standards of conduct not apply to you, as to others?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the position that the Workers' Party has advocated is the standard of governance, then, what it would mean is this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Imagine if you had a Workers' Party government, if there were to be a government official that has been found liable for something, does that person stand aside when there is an appeal pending?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The answer would be no – you just carry on, business as usual.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What kind of tone does that set for the government?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What sort of signal of governance does that convey?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Faisal Manap says, when asked what he would do with respect to the Court judgment, that he has belief in his colleagues.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I appreciate that he has belief in his colleagues.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The point is that when you have a Court judgment with these findings, what do you, as the head or the Chairman of the Town Council do?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: He also referred to the 2015 General Election and he talked about the fact that the residents have given a mandate to Mr Low Thia Khiang and to Ms Sylvia Lim in 2015.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The residents of Aljunied did give them a mandate to be their Members of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, no one is suggesting that they should stand down as town councillors.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But likewise, objecting to this Motion also speaks volumes.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As intimated by Workers' Party's Chair, Ms Sylvia Lim, insofar as the judgment referred to in the Motion is concerned, the window for appeal remains open and the PAP must explain truthfully what is its motive in hurriedly filing this Motion before the case is concluded.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: On the second limb, I will not repeat the points made by Ms Sylvia Lim on the appeal process, but I will restate that grounds of appeal can cover both issues of fact and issues of law.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, I do wish to add that the judgment also raises the real prospect of the plaintiffs, namely, PRPTC or AHTC's Independent Panel, filing an appeal against the judgment identified in the Deputy Prime Minister's Motion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This is because the plaintiffs did not succeed in many causes of action, some of which were either rejected or dismissed by the Judge.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One important example with significant repercussions for their case at the second trial on quantum being the plaintiffs' attempt to reverse the burden of proof and to put onus on the defendants to disprove loss.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: To that end, there is no reason for Parliament to be prematurely hijacked as a substitute for the judicial process when the window for appeal on the judgment has not closed.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I hope all Members, not just Nominated Members of Parliament, consider this when they decide on the Motion later.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Next, I wish to consider limbs (iii) and (iv) of the Motion.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Natural justice dictates that any question of a recusal for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang from their roles at the Town Council must surely be considered after the case is concluded.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, if Parliament passes the Motion, the councillors of AHTC, not the Workers' Party, will discuss the matter and vote on it, if that is the collective decision of the Council.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In any such decision, Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim will excuse themselves from voting on the issue and will not participate in any discussion of the matter.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: On my part, I have absolute trust and confidence in both Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang’s leadership and their continued participation on the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I speak for myself when I say that I will not be voting for them to be recused from financial matters should it be determined so by Council even if this Motion passes.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Let us not fake ignorance and say, "Wow".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It is in the judgment that has been read.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: As Chairman of the Town Council between 2011 and 2015, despite challenging circumstances and under tremendous pressure, Ms Sylvia Lim led the Town Council to manage the estate without major disruption of service affecting the lives of residents.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, as Vice Chair, has contributed much over the years to the positive transformation of the Town Council today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The accumulated surplus position and all other matters will be in that report.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
