text: That said, any decision to consider a recusal for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang is for the individual town councillors to make and AHTC will act in accordance with their decisions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For Mr Low Thia Khiang, he is a member of the estate and community liaison committee (ECLC) and does not chair any finance-related committee.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: ECLC does, however, approve expenditure for estate-related work.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang’s depth of Town Council experience and perspective as a long-standing Opposition town councillor on estate matters is very useful for ECLC.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Once again, it is only appropriate for the Town Council to take a collective decision on any recusal if it decides to do so and AHTC will act according to the Council's decisions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, the two words that have defined this Motion are "hurried" and "premature".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I would just like to follow up on a point made by Minister Indranee Rajah on what happens when such an event occurs to a government official in future.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Those will be the considerations that will be relevant.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, I reject any suggestion that the Workers' Party will not have any moral authority to question an issue like that when it comes up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And we know one issue, for example, that came up, it was December 2016, if my memory serves me right, just a few days before Christmas, knowledge of a tri-factor prosecution involving Keppel Corporation, Brazil, the US and Singapore comes to light.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Members of Parliament had slightly less than 48 hours to file a Parliamentary Question about this issue – slightly less than 48 hours.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Not a single PAP Member of Parliament filed a question on the matter, probably one of the most serious corporate issues – corporate scandals – that had affected Singapore’s Government-linked company.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, if Workers' Party Members of Parliament will have no moral authority to file any Question on a matter like that, how sure are we that a PAP Member of Parliament will file a Question?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is a question of what is the standard of governance and what is the appropriate conduct?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What is very clear is that the Workers' Party's standard of governance and conduct is very different from that of this Government's.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I just wanted to get some clarification whether I misheard the leader of the Opposition that after this matter is disposed of on appeal and that the findings stand, the leader of the Opposition, the Town Council, will not vote for the two Members against whom findings of dishonesty stand to recuse themselves from even financial decisions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Minister Desmond Lee, I think you may have misheard me.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The position has been, as I had made in my speech, any question of a recusal could actually come up any time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: One further clarification because I think I recall hearing a statement that the Town Council would do what it needs to do.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The response of the Town Council will, of course, be its own responsibility.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But let us all be clear about what we are asking in this Motion, which is calling upon the Town Council to do what we think is right.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Workers' Party's Members of Parliament, of course, may have a different view.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I do not know if I have heard him correctly, but in his speech, he was asserting that the Workers' Party Members of Parliament had allowed FMSS to charge very high rates throughout their entire incumbency as the MA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But would he not agree that, actually, even in this High Court judgment, the trial Judge did not find any breach in the award of the second MA and EMSU contract?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like him to confirm that and summarised at paragraph 12 of the Annex that the Deputy Prime Minister gave out earlier.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is that he said he was surprised we would take the position that town councillors – arguing that town councillors owed fiduciary duties as a novel point.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But does he not agree that there is actually no case law on this point and this is the first case where a Judge has actually applied his mind to this issue of whether Town Councils, in fact, owe fiduciary duties?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, in that sense, it is a novel point of law that is being argued in fact with rigour in the Court.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I had said in my speech that the auditors, PwC and KPMG, had all previously found those points about charging.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I would not go into the details on them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I am sure that Member would have read them through and through.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, these are examples of why I think, based on the nature of this civil suit finding, there is a need for the affected town councillors to take the necessary action and that, in respect of the extent of damages, if any, it is to be determined in the hearing thereafter.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for case law, I think the Member is really, playing lawyer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, case law on the legal duties of town councillors are few and far between.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This case has generated jurisprudence on the front, but I think the key point is this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Given the kind of findings of dishonesty, of subterfuge, of misleading town councillors, misleading the public and so on, found by the Court, what are the duties expected of a person in the shoes of a town councillor?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: No doubt, this may be novel from a jurisprudential point of view.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I think let us put ourselves in the shoes of Members of this House and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What do you expect of a town councillor against whom such findings have been made?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What kinds of responsibilities and standards do we have to hold ourselves to?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The Minister has still not answered my question whether he actually agrees that even in this High Court judgment, the Court has not found any breach, independent or continuing breach in the award of the second MA and EMSU contract.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Except, Sir, that the issue of findings of overcharging in terms of amount will be determined by the subsequent hearing, but what I was highlighting are the auditors' reports.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I have raised this Motion because it concerns the integrity of Members of this House.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And I have asked Ms Sylvia Lim earlier, "Is this sub judice?" And she said, "No".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We cannot stay silent when a Court finds severe lapses among Members of this House, to be characterised as "dishonest", "lacking integrity", "lacking in candour".

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Parliament is a key foundation of our political system.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Members in this House set the tone for politics that we have in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singaporeans expect more from their Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: If we let things go unanswered, Singaporeans will be right to ask what kind of a system we have today.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Whether it is a clean and incorruptible Singapore that we have worked hard to maintain all these years, whether they can trust the people whom they have elected to represent and serve them, whether the political leaders, whether from the Ruling Party or the Opposition, deserve to be trusted.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Throughout this entire saga, the Workers' Party has avoided giving any straight answers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have not explained why they went out of their way to advocate the waiver of tender and the appointment of FMSS, despite claiming that there was nothing wrong with what they did.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have not explained why FMSS was allowed to charge higher MA rates than CPG even though FMSS was run by their friends and was close to the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They have not shown responsibility towards ensuring that payments to FMSS were properly made and that they had done the necessary to protect residents' money.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are not shy to support the Motion that is critical of us but will address and remedy the issues raised by the AGO report." So, Mr Low Thia Khiang made it very clear that you are for transparency, the Workers' Party is for transparency and accountability.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You are not shy to support the Motion that is critical of the Workers' Party and that you will address and remedy the issues raised by the AGO report.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But we just heard something else from Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I ask the Workers' Party of today, "Do you stand, still stand for transparency and accountability?" In fact, I was very disappointed that Ms Sylvia Lim, at the initial stage of our Motion earlier today, chose to hide behind the ongoing appeal, despite serious concerns that the judgment has raised.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I was even more surprised that Mr Pritam Singh repeated the same point.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Now, I want to remind this House that I am asking, all that I am asking this House to do is to ask Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang two very simple questions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is the least that they can do, right?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There is no admission of guilt involved, simply whether you are prepared to give your residents some reassurance.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Ms Anthea Ong earlier on mentioned about your concern of whether this is a partisan debate.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It was the Independent Panel appointed by the Workers' Party and, about which Mr Pritam Singh said they were eminent, consisting of Senior Counsels – two Senior Counsels – and one head of an audit firm.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It was also the High Court that characterised their behaviour as dishonest, lacking in integrity, candour and transparency.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And it was the Court of Appeal that raised the question of their behaviour was of questionable legality.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, like Mr Desmond Lee, I am very troubled that Mr Faisal Manap – Mr Faisal Manap is back with us – that, essentially, the position that you are going to take was that you would ask your Independent Panel, that you are not prepared to take a decision now.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You are not prepared to take a decision.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Sadly, Mr Pritam Singh reinforced that and said that you have refused to give your residents the assurance that Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang will no longer be involved in financial matters for AHTC.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As I said in my speech earlier, this is a basic step that any company whose officers are embroiled in such a case, more so after a strongly-worded judgment has been passed, would have asked their officers to do, even a company would have done that.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: They need only to look at the example of Ang Mo Kio Town Council which my colleagues have explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And that the Government has shown that we will act against any wrongdoing no matter the party.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It does not sweep things under the carpet.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mr Faisal Manap also indicated and refused to take steps to protect public funds and to protect their residents' money.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: You are the Chairman of the Town Council now.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We may differ on where we stand on many issues, but we always assume that we have at least agreed on the nature of politics we should have in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The integrity of Workers' Party Members, the integrity of Members of Parliament, have been called into question and not addressed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In any reputable organisation, as I have said earlier, individuals who have fallen short would themselves feel a sense of shame and regret, and would themselves do the right thing, unbidden, failing which other town councillors who have done the duty and acted to cleanse their own house, failing which the political party which controls the Town Council would step in to put things right.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the case of AHTC and the Workers' Party, all these multiple levels of personal and Party responsibilities have failed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, my question is a very simple one.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: What is the right thing to do for Members of the Workers' Party?

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I think Members of this House know the answer.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Members of the Workers' Party know in their hearts the answers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, I urge the Workers' Party Members that, despite your recalcitrant stand today, after this debate, the Workers' Party and AHTC will reflect very carefully on what has happened in AHTC and what the House has been discussing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I hope that you will conclude that you should carry out your duty and do what the Motion recommends.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I urge Members of this House to take a stand on this Motion in the interest of preserving clean politics in Singapore.

text: Will hon Members who support the Division please rise in their places?
